summary: A short cover note from BBN attaching a map of the ARPANET as of the end of December 1972. The ovals show which host computers were thought to connect to each IMP, and sites were asked to report errors or changes. The map itself was a drawing and is not part of the text.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 432 introduces a logical map of the ARPANET as of December 30, 1972. It asks sites to check the map and report errors or planned changes to their connections.

subtitle: A request to review the ARPANET logical map

tldr.problem: Network sites needed a shared view of which host computers were connected to each IMP.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC attaches a logical map dated December 30, 1972, and explains what its oval symbols represent.
tldr.outcome: Sites were asked to report errors and planned connection changes to BBN or the NIC.

today: RFC 432 is a cover note for a logical map dated December 30, 1972. Its text asks sites to check the attached map and report changes.

sections.title: A Snapshot of Network Connections
sections.content:
Nancy Neigus at BBN says the attached logical map represents the ARPANET as of December 30, 1972. The map uses ovals for host computers believed to be connected to each IMP. A double oval indicates an interface.

The accompanying drawing is not included in the plain-text version of this RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The map was intended to show which hosts were connected to each IMP at the end of December 1972. Its symbols distinguish hosts and interfaces.

sections.title: Checking and Updating the Map
sections.content:
The notice asks sites to contact Nancy Neigus if the map contains errors or if their connections to hosts are expected to change in the next few months. It also asks sites to report such changes in the future.

Users could contact BBN by telephone or leave a message for NJN at the NIC.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites were asked to check their connections on the map and report mistakes or planned changes. The notice gives phone and NIC message options for contacting BBN.

sections.title: Keeping Network Information Current
sections.content: The RFC treats the map as a maintained record: sites should report changes when they occur, not only while reviewing this copy. The note contains no protocol specification; it is a coordination request tied to the attached network diagram.
sections.plainLanguage: The map could remain useful only if sites reported changes to their connections. This RFC asks for those updates rather than defining a network protocol.
